_comment: Input for scripts/split-sprites.py. Each source sheet has a standing row and a sitting row of
eight figures. The COLUMN ORDER IS NOT A ROTATION: the artwork repeats some angles and skips
others, so every column was classified by eye (2026-09-26) by which way the BODY faces --
knees, belly, chair back -- with the camera looking north (south = facing the viewer,
east = facing screen right). Change a column here and re-run the script to correct a call.
A direction the sheet does not contain is filled by mirroring its opposite ('mirror'), and
sprite.json records which files are mirrors. Unused columns are listed so nothing is lost.
The sheet's seated row is drawn ~10% smaller than its standing row, so a seated sprite gets its
own scale: seated head-top = sittingHeightRatio x standing height (0.72 is typical for an adult
on an office chair). Still one uniform scale per frame; nothing is stretched.

standing._notes: Complete. Column 8's body faces southwest; his head is turned back toward the camera.

_unused.7: west by the body, but the head faces east

standing._notes: Column 6's body faces northwest; her head is turned back over her shoulder.
